description: The checklist of a change. Record it before the build, in one lite checklist call. The base app runs and does not have the change. Study the ticket, the docs, and the base app first. Do not test the change before the build.

objective.description: What to verify, in one sentence.

criteria.description: The count of numbered acceptance criteria in the ticket. Use 0 when the ticket has none.

items.description: The rules to verify. Write one item for each numbered acceptance criterion. Then add the existing rules near the change that the change can break: the same totals and calculations, the same validation and error messages, the lists, exports, and counters that show the changed data, the permissions, and the rules in the docs for the same page or endpoint.

questions.description: One question for each point that the ticket and the docs do not settle: a threshold and whether it is inclusive, rounding, how two rules combine, the order of operations, and the result after a state change. Also ask when the base value and the documented value differ. The PM answers before the build. Leave out this field when you have no question.

examples.objective: Verify the new loan limit and the existing late fees.

items.text: A member can have at most 5 books on loan.
A late return adds a fee of 0.50 for each day.

baseline.steps: Return loan L1 3 days late. Then GET /api/loans/L1.

questions.question: Is a sixth loan refused, or put on a waiting list?

id.description: A unique item ID, for example R1.

source.description: The file that states the rule: the ticket file for a criterion, or docs/<file>#<section> for an existing rule.

criterion.description: The number of the acceptance criterion of this item. Give it only on a criterion item. Do not merge two criteria in one item.

baseline.description: Give a baseline to each existing rule that the change can break. Measure it on the base app with one request or a few steps, not a full test. An item with a baseline is a regression item. Each build must measure it again.

steps.description: The exact request or UI steps. Each build does these steps again.

value.description: The value that you saw on the base app. Use a short exact value, for example 409 "Book is on loan" or fee 1.50.

documented.description: The value that the docs state. When it is not the base value, add a question.
